answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable deposit before it may submit jobs or vote; rewards and voting weight then accrue only to that bonded identity. Splitting one agent into many sybils does not multiply its influence without multiplying the capital at risk, and proven fraud forfeits the bond. The atlas registry can record each bond, while pearl and nebula are example agent names, not trust signals. This raises the attacker's upfront cost and makes successful deception economically costly.
